problem: Original ByteTrack includes Lost tracks in high-score association, but its low-score stage includes only unmatched currently Tracked objects. A reappearing weak fish can remain structurally ineligible for its old identity even when current body correspondences support that identity.
scope: Explicit evidence-based recovery route after original association and before creating a new identity; not a silent change to the original baseline graph
source: Most recent valid object observation among causal lags1,2,4,8; co-visible identity protection may retain a genuinely distinct Lost object
target: Actual current unclaimed proposals with score>=0.3, initially restricted to score<=0.6
constraints: Valid surviving body points; distinct current candidate ownership; one-to-one assignment between Lost identities and unclaimed observations; preserve original25-frame maximum age
update: Reactivate the original identity using the actual current observation; never synthesize a detection, revise an earlier output or assign a new ID to an already recoverable old object
ablations: No object history beyond latest observation
sequence: Original update, credible old-identity recovery, then optional three-image cycle-confirmed birth
selection: Full Dev only; no Test score selects any configuration
novelty_status: Proposed recoverability mechanism, no contribution credit before complete removal/IR controls and all7 Test videos. Hungarian assignment and object memory are classical components, not novel alone.
